[Listing] Integrate Import Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN listings/import flow (src/pages/listings, src/pages/listings-detail) pulls tours that already exist on GoThru into the app, via the listings API (apil.gothru.co). See docs/analyze.md SS2.6 (listings), SS3.4 (backend), and the projects/panoramas data model in SS3.3.

Goal

Implement "Import Tour" in the Flutter app: fetch a tour that exists on GoThru (server-side) and import it into the local store so it can be opened/edited like a local project.

Scope

  • Trigger import for a selected server tour (from the listing/import screen).
  • Fetch the tour's data from GoThru (project metadata, panoramas, connections, levels).
  • Persist into the local DB (projects, panoramas, connections, levels) and download required image assets to the Panorama folder.
  • Progress feedback during import; the imported tour appears in the local project list.
  • Mark imported panoramas as already existing on GoThru (gothru_exist / uploaded) to avoid re-upload.

Out of Scope

  • Listing the available server tours (separate task: [Listing] Integrate list tour).
  • Editing/uploading after import; moderation.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Importing a server tour creates the corresponding projects/panoramas/connections/levels rows locally.
  • Required panorama assets are downloaded locally and render in the imported tour.
  • Imported panoramas are flagged as present on GoThru (not queued for re-upload).
  • Import shows progress and a clear success/failure result.
  • Re-importing the same tour does not create duplicates.
  • Works with the signed-in session token; errors surfaced (no silent failure).

Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 - TC-8: See the original developer scenarios above.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: locally-created tours are unaffected by imports.

[Listing] Integrate List Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN listings screen (src/pages/listings) fetches the signed-in user's tours from GoThru via the listings API (apil.gothru.co) and displays them for browsing/import. See docs/analyze.md §2.6 and §3.4.

Goal

Implement the server tour list (Listing) in the Flutter app: fetch and display the signed-in user's tours that exist on GoThru, as the browse surface from which a user picks a tour to import.

Scope

  • Fetch the user's GoThru tours (listing API) for the current session.
  • Render a scrollable list with per-tour basics (name/title, thumbnail/cover, address, status, panorama count where available).
  • Pagination / lazy loading for large accounts; pull-to-refresh.
  • Loading, empty, and error states.
  • Each item exposes an entry point to import (pairs with [Listing] Integrate Import Tour).

Out of Scope

  • The import action/persistence itself (separate task: [Listing] Integrate Import Tour).
  • Editing/deleting server tours.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The list fetches and displays the user's GoThru tours for the current session.
  • Each item shows name, cover/thumbnail, and key metadata (address/status/count where available).
  • Pagination/lazy load works for large accounts; pull-to-refresh re-fetches.
  • Loading / empty / error states handled.
  • Tapping a tour leads to the import entry point.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — List server tours (happy path)

  1. Sign in → open the Listing screen.
  2. Expected: The user's GoThru tours load and display with titles/thumbnails.

TC-2 — Empty account

  1. View the listing for an account with no server tours.
  2. Expected: Clear empty state; no stuck spinner or crash.

TC-3 — Pagination / large list

  1. View an account with many tours; scroll to the bottom.
  2. Expected: More tours load (lazy load/pagination); smooth scrolling.

TC-4 — Pull-to-refresh

  1. Pull to refresh the list.
  2. Expected: List re-fetches and reflects current server state.

TC-5 — Network / API error

  1. Go offline or simulate API failure.
  2. Expected: Clear error state with retry; no crash.

TC-6 — Metadata correctness

  1. Compare list items against the GoThru account.
  2. Expected: Names/covers/metadata match the server.

TC-7 — Entry to import

  1. Tap a tour in the list.
  2. Expected: Navigates to the import entry point for that tour.

TC-8 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels/states translated; no raw keys.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: local project list is separate from and unaffected by the server tour list.

[Level] Integrate Add Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN multi-level support — the levels table groups panoramas into floors/levels (docs/analyze.md §2.4, §3.3: levels = level_name, level_type, position, folder_id, project_id). Pairs with the Default Level task.

Goal

Implement "Add Level" in Tour Detail: let the user create a new level for the current project, persisted to the local levels table.

Scope

  • Add-level action with a form (level name/type; auto-assigned position).
  • Insert a levels row for the project; new level appears in the level list/selector.
  • Validation (e.g. required name, no invalid duplicates); localized labels.

Out of Scope

  • Editing/deleting/reordering levels (separate tasks); moving panoramas between levels (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can add a new level with name/type.
  • A levels row is created with correct project_id and a sensible position.
  • New level shows immediately in the level list/selector.
  • Validation prevents empty/invalid level creation.
  • Works offline; survives app restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Add a level (happy path)

  1. Open a tour → Levels → Add Level → enter name → save.
  2. Expected: New level appears in the list/selector.

TC-2 — Validation

  1. Try to add a level with an empty name.
  2. Expected: Inline error; level not created.

TC-3 — Ordering

  1. Add several levels.
  2. Expected: Each gets a correct position; list order is consistent.

TC-4 — Persistence after restart

  1. Add a level, relaunch, reopen the tour.
  2. Expected: The level persists.

TC-5 — Offline

  1. Add a level offline.
  2. Expected: Created locally with no network error.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language and add a level.
  2. Expected: Labels/validation translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: existing default level and panorama assignments unaffected.

[Level] Integrate List Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN level list (src/components/level-local) renders a project's levels ordered by position; see docs/analyze.md §2.4, §3.3 (levels).

Goal

Implement the level list in Tour Detail: load and display the current project's levels (ordered), as the surface the other level actions (add/edit/delete/change) operate on.

Scope

  • Query levels for the open project from the local DB.
  • Render levels ordered by position, showing name/type and panorama count per level where available.
  • Loading, empty, and error states; list refreshes when levels change.
  • Selecting a level filters/scopes the panorama view to that level.

Out of Scope

  • Add/Edit/Delete/Change-level actions (separate tasks) — this provides the list they plug into.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Tour Detail shows the project's levels ordered by position.
  • Each level shows name/type and (where available) its panorama count.
  • Selecting a level scopes the panorama list to that level.
  • Loading / empty / error states handled.
  • List reflects add/edit/delete changes without restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — List levels (happy path)

  1. Open a tour with multiple levels.
  2. Expected: Levels render in correct position order with names.

TC-2 — Single/default level

  1. Open a tour with only the default level.
  2. Expected: One level listed; no crash/empty glitch.

TC-3 — Panorama count

  1. View levels that contain different numbers of panoramas.
  2. Expected: Per-level counts are correct.

TC-4 — Select level filters panoramas

  1. Tap a level.
  2. Expected: Panorama list scopes to that level.

TC-5 — Reflects changes

  1. Add/rename/delete a level (via those flows) and return.
  2. Expected: The list updates immediately.

TC-6 — Offline / persistence

  1. Open levels offline; relaunch and reopen.
  2. Expected: Levels render from local DB; consistent after restart.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: listing levels does not modify level/panorama data.

[Level] Integrate Edit Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN level management (src/components/level-local) — levels fields level_name, level_type, position (docs/analyze.md §3.3).

Goal

Implement "Edit Level" in Tour Detail: rename/edit a level's properties (name, type, and optionally order/position), persisted to the local levels table.

Scope

  • Edit action on a level, pre-filled with current values.
  • Update the levels row (level_name, level_type, and position if reordering is in scope here).
  • Validation; changes reflected immediately in the level list.

Out of Scope

  • Add/Delete levels (separate tasks); moving panoramas between levels (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Edit form pre-populates from the selected level.
  • Saved changes persist to the levels row.
  • Validation prevents empty/invalid values.
  • Updated level reflected immediately in the list; works offline.

[Level] Integrate Delete Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN level management — deleting a level must handle the panoramas assigned to it (docs/analyze.md §3.3: panoramas.level_id, levels).

Goal

Implement "Delete Level" in Tour Detail: remove a level with a confirmation step, defining clear handling for panoramas that belong to the deleted level (reassign to the default level rather than orphaning/deleting them).

Scope

  • Delete action on a level (with confirm dialog).
  • On confirm: remove the levels row; reassign its panoramas to the default level (do not delete panoramas).
  • Prevent deleting the last/default level (guard), or define the agreed fallback.
  • Level list updates immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Deleting panoramas (separate task); add/edit levels (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Deleting a level prompts for confirmation.
  • On confirm: level removed; its panoramas reassigned to the default level (not lost).
  • The default/last level cannot be deleted (or agreed fallback applies).
  • List updates immediately; works offline; survives restart.
  • Cancel leaves everything unchanged.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Delete an empty level (happy path)

  1. Levels → select a level with no panoramas → Delete → confirm.
  2. Expected: Level removed from the list.

TC-2 — Delete a level with panoramas

  1. Delete a level that contains panoramas → confirm.
  2. Expected: Level removed; its panoramas now appear under the default level (none deleted).

TC-3 — Cancel delete

  1. Tap delete, then cancel.
  2. Expected: Nothing changes.

TC-4 — Guard default/last level

  1. Attempt to delete the only/default level.
  2. Expected: Blocked with a clear message (or agreed fallback).

TC-5 — Persistence after restart

  1. Delete a level, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Level stays deleted; reassigned panoramas persist.

TC-6 — No orphans

  1. After deleting a level with panoramas, inspect the data.
  2. Expected: No panoramas left with a dangling level_id.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: other levels and their panoramas unaffected.

[Level] Integrate Change Level Panorama (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN move-level flow (src/components/level-local/.../move-level) reassigns a panorama's level_id; see docs/analyze.md §2.4, §3.3 (panoramas.level_id).

Goal

Implement "Change Level" for a panorama in Tour Detail: move one (or more) panoramas from their current level to another level, updating panoramas.level_id locally.

Scope

  • Action to move a panorama to a different level (level picker of the project's levels).
  • Update panoramas.level_id (support multi-select where practical).
  • Panorama list / level grouping reflect the move immediately.
  • Localized labels; offline-capable.

Out of Scope

  • Add/edit/delete levels (separate tasks); reordering panoramas within a level.

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can move a panorama to another level via a picker.
  • panoramas.level_id updates to the chosen level.
  • The panorama now appears under the target level (and not the old one).
  • Works offline; survives restart; supports multi-select if implemented.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Move a panorama (happy path)

  1. Select a panorama → Change Level → pick another level.
  2. Expected: Panorama moves to the target level; removed from the source level.

TC-2 — Move to same level (no-op)

  1. Choose the panorama's current level.
  2. Expected: No change / graceful no-op; no duplication.

TC-3 — Multi-select move (if supported)

  1. Select multiple panoramas → move to a level.
  2. Expected: All move correctly to the target level.

TC-4 — Grouping reflects move

  1. After moving, view the level list / grouped panorama view.
  2. Expected: Counts and grouping update immediately.

TC-5 — Persistence after restart

  1. Move a panorama, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: The panorama stays on the target level.

TC-6 — Offline

  1. Perform the move offline.
  2. Expected: Updates locally with no network error.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: moving a panorama does not alter its image/connections, only its level_id.
